details.injected_rule: When designing module interfaces or dependencies, explicitly verify that required inputs (such as baseline metrics or return values) are available from the specified source modules before listing them, because assuming data flow without confirming the actual function signature leads to unimplementable modules and broken cross-file dependencies.

When designing a module interface, define all shared constants and parameters as public module-level exports before implementation begins, because consumers require direct access to these values for data interpretation and consistency, not just function inputs.

When designing new modules that rely on existing infrastructure, prioritize and explicitly depend on existing modules to satisfy functional requirements rather than creating duplicate wrappers or parallel implementations, because reusing existing sources prevents structural ambiguity and violates the 'One concept, one place' principle.
